searchText: Hi everyone, I wanted to do some local `devnet-6` testing combining EthereumJS with lighthouse (took https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/releases/tag/v7.0.0-beta.5) without usage of wrapper-tooling like Docker/Ansible/Kubernetes or the like. Basically running this command: ```shell lighthouse beacon_node \ --datadir=./datadir \ --testnet-dir=./network-config \ --allow-insecure-genesis-sync \ --execution-endpoint=http://localhost:8551 \ --execution-jwt=/Users/USERNAME/Library/Ethereum/ethereumjs/jwtsecret \ --boot-nodes=enr:-Iq4QGEKWSmZX2L5BxnnLyV1lqmgb-GxWXj-DUe50ILbXzMxTfL4YVHLOqRDrlQ9XmN-JUEt_qOqSjy023N4BWTCyi6GAZTMP2G2gmlkgnY0gmlwhLympd-Jc2VjcDI1NmsxoQJJ3h8aUO3GJHv-bdvHtsQZ2OEisutelYfGjXO4lSg8BYN1ZHCCIzI,MORE_NODES ``` with `network-config` being a reference to https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets/tree/master/network-configs/devnet-6/metadata and bootnodes taken as a comma-separated list from https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets/blob/master/network-configs/devnet-6/metadata/bootstrap_nodes.txt, EL <-> CL connection gets established. I am now just **not getting peers** on the lighthouse side. Anyone ad-hoc spotting what I am doing wrong? any reason you aren't using kurtosis? I prefer to have direct control over everything, not totally against though. So where would I start then? There isn't any Kurtosis reference here https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets if I am not mistaken. ```yaml participants: - el_type: ethereumjs el_image: ethpandaops/ethereumjs:master cl_type: lighthouse cl_image: sigp/lighthouse:v7.0.0-beta.5 network_params: network: pectra-devnet-6 checkpoint_sync_enabled: true checkpoint_sync_url: https://checkpoint-sync.pectra-devnet-6.ethpandaops.io ``` you can just specify that you want to use pectra-devnet-6 as your network and it should get all the info from our repos forgot that you need to enable checkpoint sync too. I'll probably set that as default for devnets Can you give me a dummy-first-round-pointer? So I would roughly... 1. Install/setup/understand Kurtosis from https://github.com/kurtosis-tech/kurtosis 2. Clone https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets (do I need to setup anything from there as well?) and then... 3. Run some Kurtosis command against some file from the `pectra-devnets` repo? Is this roughly correct? Step1: install kt: https://docs.kurtosis.com/install Step2: Save the file under file.yaml Step3: `kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file file.yaml --image-download always` no need to clone anything, just have that above mentioned yaml file saved locally so you can reference it What is "the file" from step 2? and you can also use your local branch if you build a docker image locally this is file.yaml Ah, so that's self-contained? No extract from some `pectra-devnets` file? its done automatically 😄 it fetches all the network params and bootnode info automagically Ok, I guess I might be able to do that! Thanks a lot! 🙏 🙂 👍

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content:
Hi everyone, I wanted to do some local `devnet-6` testing combining EthereumJS with lighthouse (took https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/releases/tag/v7.0.0-beta.5) without usage of wrapper-tooling like Docker/Ansible/Kubernetes or the like.

Basically running this command:

```shell
lighthouse beacon_node \
  --datadir=./datadir \
  --testnet-dir=./network-config \
  --allow-insecure-genesis-sync \
  --execution-endpoint=http://localhost:8551 \
  --execution-jwt=/Users/USERNAME/Library/Ethereum/ethereumjs/jwtsecret \
  --boot-nodes=enr:-Iq4QGEKWSmZX2L5BxnnLyV1lqmgb-GxWXj-DUe50ILbXzMxTfL4YVHLOqRDrlQ9XmN-JUEt_qOqSjy023N4BWTCyi6GAZTMP2G2gmlkgnY0gmlwhLympd-Jc2VjcDI1NmsxoQJJ3h8aUO3GJHv-bdvHtsQZ2OEisutelYfGjXO4lSg8BYN1ZHCCIzI,MORE_NODES
```

with `network-config` being a reference to https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets/tree/master/network-configs/devnet-6/metadata and bootnodes taken as a comma-separated list from https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets/blob/master/network-configs/devnet-6/metadata/bootstrap_nodes.txt, EL <-> CL connection gets established.

I am now just **not getting peers** on the lighthouse side. Anyone ad-hoc spotting what I am doing wrong?

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: any reason you aren't using kurtosis?

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content: I prefer to have direct control over everything, not totally against though. So where would I start then?

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content: There isn't any Kurtosis reference here https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets if I am not mistaken.

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content:
```yaml
participants:
  - el_type: ethereumjs
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethereumjs:master
    cl_type: lighthouse
    cl_image: sigp/lighthouse:v7.0.0-beta.5
network_params:
  network: pectra-devnet-6
checkpoint_sync_enabled: true
checkpoint_sync_url: https://checkpoint-sync.pectra-devnet-6.ethpandaops.io
```

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: you can just specify that you want to use pectra-devnet-6 as your network and it should get all the info from our repos

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: forgot that you need to enable checkpoint sync too. I'll probably set that as default for devnets

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content:
Can you give me a dummy-first-round-pointer? So I would roughly...
1. Install/setup/understand Kurtosis from https://github.com/kurtosis-tech/kurtosis
2. Clone https://github.com/ethpandaops/pectra-devnets (do I need to setup anything from there as well?) and then...
3. Run some Kurtosis command against some file from the `pectra-devnets` repo?

Is this roughly correct?

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content:
Step1: install kt: https://docs.kurtosis.com/install
Step2: Save the file under file.yaml
Step3: `kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file file.yaml --image-download always`

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: no need to clone anything, just have that above mentioned yaml file saved locally so you can reference it

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: and you can also use your local branch if you build a docker image locally

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content: Ah, so that's self-contained? No extract from some `pectra-devnets` file?

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: it fetches all the network params and bootnode info automagically

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content: Ok, I guess I might be able to do that! Thanks a lot! 🙏 🙂
